description: An envelope follower: it tracks how far a signal swings and gives out both that envelope and its mirror image, for ducking one sound under another

params.text: Sets how fast the envelope falls, 0 to 10, the figure being the volts per second taken off the envelope while the input is below it
Bends the fall, -10 to +10; the rate is multiplied by e raised to this number times the seconds since the last peak, so a positive setting accelerates the fall and a negative one flattens it out
Scales the envelope, 0 passing it through unchanged and 1 multiplying it by ten, with the result limited to 10V

inputs.text: The signal followed; its sign is discarded before use, so the envelope climbs to the size of the largest swing in either direction

outputs.text: The envelope taken away from 10V, so it drops as the input grows; patch it to a VCA to duck one signal under another

notes: decay arrives at 0, and at 0 the envelope never falls: it climbs to the largest swing so far and holds there. Turn decay up before expecting an envelope shape.
once the input has been within 0.01V of zero for one second, out is forced to 0V and inv to 10V, whatever the envelope had reached.
both outputs take their channel count from the input jack, so with nothing patched they carry no channels at all.

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
